description: Width tiers for Dance — Years 1-2 band
subject: Dance

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Y1-2 Dance, minimum is typically one choreographic context, one performance occasion, or one cultural dance observation — sufficient to demonstrate the capability.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope covering the range of elaboration examples — what a well-taught Y1-2 student would experience across the band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts, stimuli types, cultural communities or collaborative configurations. All First Nations elaborations appear in wider.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Y1-2 elaborations are dance-strand specific — all five dance descriptors have dedicated elaborations at this band.

AC9ADA2C01.minimum_width: Use at least two elements of dance to choreograph a sequence with beginning, middle and end in response to one stimulus — can name the elements used.
AC9ADA2C01.typical_width: Choreograph dance sequences using improvised movement in response to diverse stimuli (weather, music, stories, imagery, movement exploration of body mechanics); share and learn movements collaboratively with a partner; combine and extend ideas into a sequence; use learnt terminology to discuss the work; incorporate constructive feedback.
wider: Use student-created music (rhythmic patterns, body percussion) as the primary choreographic stimulus — applying time and dynamics elements in direct response to the music
Choreograph a sequence communicating care for a place that is important to the student — using element choices to express relationship and responsibility for Country/Place
Teach improvised movements to a partner, learn their movements in return, and combine collaboratively — developing each other's material to create an extended sequence
elaborations: using improvised movements to create a dance sequence that represents a weather event, or shows how they might take care of a place that is important to them
using music they have created as inspiration for a dance
devising a starting shape, a way of moving to another place, and combining ideas with a partner
using ideas from exploration of balance, posture, and body part movement to create a dance sequence
using patterns of locomotor movements, sharing these with a partner, and working collaboratively to combine and extend
using own words and learnt dance terminology and recognising constructive feedback

AC9ADA2D01.minimum_width: Demonstrate safe movement in a defined space with awareness of others; explore at least three fundamental movements — varying one quality in each.
AC9ADA2D01.typical_width: Develop habitual safe dance awareness; use improvisation to explore movement possibilities in response to varied stimuli (imagery, music, shared stories); explore fundamental locomotor and non-locomotor movements at multiple levels and directions; move in open and crowded spaces; use Viewpoints questions to develop metacognitive awareness of movement choices.
wider: Explore movement inspired by natural phenomena (falling leaf, gliding bird, rolling log) — attending to dynamics and control in sustained exploration
Use Viewpoints questions systematically: 'What levels are you using?', 'Can you use a different body part?', 'What direction could you travel?' — as a self-directed movement inquiry tool
Practise safe movement in varied spatial configurations (small groups, scattered, lines) — building adaptable spatial awareness across different density conditions
elaborations: developing awareness of and taking responsibility for safe dance practice
using improvisation to explore movement possibilities in response to stimuli
using Viewpoints to ask questions and identify movement possibilities
exploring fundamental movements safely to develop ideas based on familiar situations
moving around open and crowded spaces safely; identifying distance between self and others; using props; reflecting on safe and unsafe movement

AC9ADA2E01.minimum_width: Observe one dance from an unfamiliar cultural context; describe at least two features using own words and one dance term; identify one reason why people dance in that context.
AC9ADA2E01.typical_width: Explore where, why and how people across cultures and communities experience dance; use Viewpoints questions to observe and describe movement, costume, music and communication; identify cultural purposes (stories, traditions, ceremonies); recognise patterns of movement using learnt terminology; identify how dance communicates feelings about places, people and experiences.
wider: Share dances familiar from students' own home and family contexts — comparing purposes and traditions with dances shared by peers, building a collective picture of the class community's dance diversity
Investigate how dance communicates feelings about specific places or environments — connecting to students' own sense of belonging and relationship to place
Explore dances from two different cultural contexts students have not previously encountered — comparing purpose, movement style, and what they communicate
elaborations: identifying features of dances that communicate cultural knowledge such as stories, traditions or ceremonies
using Viewpoints to ask questions about dances experienced
recognising and describing patterns of movement using own words and learnt terminology
identifying similarities and differences in dances by sharing, viewing and learning dances from families and communities
identifying how dance can show what feelings people have about places, people or experiences

AC9ADA2E02.minimum_width: Identify at least one occasion when First Nations Australians use dance and explain one reason why; observe one First Nations Australian dance and describe at least one element used.
AC9ADA2E02.typical_width: Explore when, where, how and why First Nations Australians use dance to share cultural knowledge; identify dances at school, in community, and in national events; observe element use in First Nations Australian dance using learnt vocabulary; explore movements with community representatives or via co-created resources.
wider: Work with a First Nations Australian community member who has cultural authority to co-create movements representing shapes and patterns from their interpretations of the night sky — experiencing dance as a vehicle for First Nations knowledge transmission

Investigate how First Nations Australians observe protocols and respect Elders and knowledge holders at cultural events where dance is performed — noticing what these protocols communicate about cultural values
Compare element use across two different First Nations Australian dance examples from different communities or occasions
elaborations: exploring when, where, how and why First Nations Australians use dance during celebrations and significant occasions
observing how the elements of dance are used in First Nations Australian choreography and/or performance
identifying where dance occurs in First Nations Australians' cultural expressions and noting audience protocols
learning about First Nations Australians' interpretations of the night sky and co-creating movements with cultural authority holders

AC9ADA2P01.minimum_width: Present a dance sequence to the class in an informal setting; use at least one intentional expressive quality; respond to one Viewpoints question about the performance.
AC9ADA2P01.typical_width: Share dance sequences in informal class settings — performing learned sequences, co-created dances, and sequences using expressive movement qualities; express ideas through movement (contrasting dynamics, movement qualities communicating ideas); use Viewpoints questions to reflect on choreography and performance.
wider: Perform a dance co-created with a First Nations Australian person who has cultural authority — following protocols for Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property use
Perform a dance for an audience beyond the immediate class (another class, a school event) — experiencing the shift in performance presence and awareness that different audience contexts create
Use Viewpoints questions to set a specific performance development goal — revisiting the performance and evaluating progress against the goal
elaborations: presenting a learned sequence or performing dances learnt to peers and teachers
performing a dance co-created with a First Nations Australian person with cultural authority, following ICIP protocols
expressing ideas through movement — contrasting dynamics, movement qualities communicating ideas
using Viewpoints to develop questions when responding to dances to reflect on choreography and performance
